newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank fix seen as positive signal to crown.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank fix seen as positive signal to crown.

text.p: The Slovak central bank (NBS) on Tuesday fixed the crown stronger against the market in a move seen by dealers as a signal of the NBS's support for the crown.

The NBS fixed the crown at 33.228 to the dollar, and at 19.617 to the mark, implying a deviation -0.78 percent versus the mark/dollar basket midpoint, while the crown was trading on the interbank market at -0.93 versus the basket.
Dealers welcomed the central bank's fixing, saying it should prevent further speculative moves counting on further weakening.
"These days the NBS has been intervening in support of the crown early which is certainly a good sign. But we will have to see how the market reacts," Peter Koprna of Slovenska Sporitelna said.
Added Tibor Fratrik of ING: "This move should at least halt speculative weakening of the crown, signs of which were seen in early trading."
The Slovak crown sharply weakened in nervous Tuesday morning activity as some $100 million left the country with dealers saying the currency could decline further before the NBS fixing.
The crown moved to around -1.40 percent against the mark/dollar basket parity from open at around 70 basis points on the depreciation side of the basket midpoint.

Fratrik said he did not expect significant changes in the crown rate until the situation on the Czech money market settled down, while Koprna said he saw room for strenghtening of the crown later on Tuesday.
